anchor: GS3.1 Indian economy: monetary policy operations and liquidity management
argumentsAgainst: A VRRR auction is a short-term liquidity-management operation, not by itself evidence of a change in the monetary-policy stance.
The notified amount is an auction ceiling or intended operation size; the record does not establish the amount actually absorbed or the auction cut-off rate.
The supplied record does not identify the specific source, size, or persistence of the liquidity conditions reviewed by the RBI.
argumentsFor: The RBI can use a variable-rate auction to absorb liquidity through market-based bidding rather than relying only on a fixed administered rate.
A one-day tenor with reversal on the following day allows fine-tuning while limiting the duration of the operation.
The operation can help align money-market liquidity conditions with the RBI’s broader monetary-policy framework, though the supplied record does not quantify its effect.

indiaImplications: Short-term liquidity absorption can influence overnight money-market conditions and the transmission of the policy stance.
Banks and other eligible participants must assess the opportunity cost of placing funds with the RBI against lending or investing elsewhere.
The one-day structure supports flexibility, but repeated operations could signal continuing liquidity-management needs; the supplied record does not establish whether such repetition is planned.
Market interpretation should distinguish an operational auction from a formal change in policy rates or stance.

officialFacts.text: The Reserve Bank decided to conduct a Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.
The notified amount for the auction was ₹50,000 crore.
The tenor of the auction was 1 day.
The auction window was 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM.
The date of reversal was November 19, 2026 (Thursday).
The operational guidelines for the auction remain the same as those given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2019-2020/1947 dated February 13, 2020.

example.heading: Illustration: temporary liquidity absorption
example.text: Suppose eligible participants place funds with the RBI in a one-day VRRR auction. Those funds would be temporarily unavailable for other uses during the tenor and would return on the stated reversal date. This is only a hypothetical illustration; the source record does not report actual bids, allotment, or outcomes.

sections.heading: Scheduled operation and timing
paragraphs: The RBI announced a Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction after reviewing current and evolving liquidity conditions. The notified amount was ₹50,000 crore, the tenor was one day, the auction window was 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM on November 18, 2026, and reversal was scheduled for November 19, 2026.
The short tenor makes the operation a temporary instrument. The source confirms the schedule, but not bids, allotment, cut-off rate, or the amount ultimately absorbed.

sections.heading: Mechanism and interpretation
paragraphs: A reverse-repo-type operation temporarily places participating funds with the RBI, reducing liquidity available to participants during the tenor; a variable-rate auction allows the rate to be discovered through bidding. The operation can therefore fine-tune short-term liquidity conditions.

The announcement should not automatically be read as a policy-rate change. The source records an operational decision and continuation of previously referenced guidelines, but does not state a change in the RBI’s policy stance.

sourceTitle: RBI to conduct Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction under LAF on November 18, 2026
staticDefinition: A Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction is a market-based short-term liquidity operation in which eligible participants bid to place funds with the RBI at variable rates for a specified tenor; the operation temporarily absorbs liquidity, with funds reversed at maturity.
use: Use the VRRR as an example of the RBI’s operational toolkit for fine-tuning short-term liquidity under the LAF, while distinguishing temporary liquidity management from a formal change in the policy rate or monetary-policy stance.

advisory_notes: The definition that VRRR uses eligible participants and market-based bidding is sound but is background analysis rather than text established by this announcement.
The claim that VRRR directly aligns money-market conditions with the policy framework is reasonable, but should remain qualified as a possible effect.
The statement that participating funds become unavailable for other uses during the tenor is a mechanism-based illustration, not an outcome reported by the source.
The claim that banks and other eligible participants face an opportunity cost is analytical and should not be presented as a source-reported consequence.
The implication that short-term liquidity absorption influences transmission is plausible but may depend on auction uptake and prevailing market conditions.
The syllabus labels GS3.1 and GS3.2 are internal taxonomy rather than official UPSC codes; the monetary-policy and liquidity-management anchor is substantively relevant to GS3.
The headline and pocketRead correctly describe a scheduled operation, but the date is future-dated in the supplied record and should be refreshed before publication.
The proposed mains question is relevant, though its assertion of competitive rate discovery should be supported by the referenced operational guidelines when teaching the mechanism.

wayForward: Interpret VRRR announcements alongside auction results, money-market rates, system-liquidity indicators, and the RBI’s formal monetary-policy communication.
Maintain clear communication separating operational liquidity management from changes in the policy stance.
Use appropriately calibrated auction size and tenor so that liquidity is fine-tuned without creating avoidable market volatility.
Evaluate outcomes rather than assuming that the notified amount equals actual liquidity absorption.
whyInNews: The Reserve Bank of India announced on November 17, 2026 that it would conduct a one-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility on November 18, 2026. The notified amount was ₹50,000 crore, with bidding from 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM and reversal scheduled for November 19, 2026.
